artists.biography: Knifeworld is the new band from Kavus Torabi (Cardiacs, The Monsoon Bassoon, Guapo). The forthcoming album also features a handful of special guests, including Ben Jacobs (Max Tundra) on trumpet, Melanie Woods (Sidi Bou Said, Cardiacs) on vocals, Katharine Blake (Miranda Sex Garden, Mediæval Bæbes) on recorders, Sarah Measures (The Monsoon Bassoon, Mothlite) on horns and flute, and Khyam Allami on drums. Pissed Up On Brake Fluid, the first Knifeworld single, will be released by Believers Roast on July 13th 2009. It is probably the closest thing to a 'straightforward rock song' Torabi has ever written. The B-side, Happy Half-life, Dear Friend is not. It's barely even rock. It is, however, extremely psychedelic. Forthcoming debut album, Buried Alone: Tales Of Crushing Defeat, is a sprawling psychedelic meisterwork, taking in elements of pop, heavy rock, hardcore, avant-progressive and folk, and is due out on August 10th 2009. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Buried Alone: Tales Of Crushing Defeat is a 2009 studio album by Knifeworld, released on the Believers Roast label. The album showcases the band's crossover progressive rock sound, blending heavy instrumentation with complex compositional structures. Spanning eleven tracks including "Singled Out For Battery," "The Wretched Fathoms," and "Corpses Feuding Underground," the record demonstrates Knifeworld's commitment to densely layered arrangements and unconventional song titles that reflect the album's thematic preoccupation with defeat and dissolution.

The album represents a significant entry in Knifeworld's discography, establishing their approach to progressive rock that incorporates heavier elements and experimental production choices. The track listing—which progresses from aggressive opener "Singled Out For Battery" through introspective pieces like "An Arrival" and concludes with "Me to the Future of You"—suggests a conceptual arc that complements the album's thematic framework. The band's willingness to merge accessibility with progressive complexity positions the work within the broader landscape of contemporary art rock.

While specific critical reception details are limited in available documentation, the album's release across multiple formats including vinyl and CD indicates a committed fanbase within the progressive rock community. The work has maintained presence in progressive music archives and streaming platforms, suggesting sustained interest among listeners of experimental and crossover rock music.
